name: study-companion
label: Study Companion
tagline: A Jan tutor grounded in your course notes

manifest.summary: Drop in lecture slides, notes or any course PDF/text and chat with Jan about them. Jan only ever answers from the material you loaded plus whatever it's told in the system prompt -- it never improvises new syllabus content. Can generate practice quizzes (question + full worked solution) grounded in a chosen source, and can plot a function on request via a PLOT directive the frontend renders as a real chart.

features.name: Sources
features.description: Any .txt/.md dropped into a course's folder under ~/Forge/apps/study-companion/data/<course>/ is picked up automatically -- no code change. Text extracted from PDFs with pdftotext works well; the app does not parse PDFs itself.

features.name: Grounded chat
features.description: Every request sends Jan the full text of the selected source(s) plus a system prompt that instructs it to answer only from that material and say plainly when something isn't covered, rather than inventing content.

features.name: Quiz generator
features.description: Asks Jan for N questions in strict JSON (question + full worked solution) from a chosen source; rendered as reveal-to-check cards. A malformed response is shown as an error rather than guessed at.

features.name: Graphing
features.description: Jan can end a reply with a PLOT block (function + domain); the frontend evaluates it with a small safe expression parser and draws a real canvas chart -- the model describes the function, the app draws it, so a hallucinated curve isn't possible.

services: Jan (http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1) -- required for chat and quizzes; the app shows a clear offline state without it
known_gaps: No PDF parsing built in -- source files must already be .txt/.md (pdftotext -layout works well).

No retrieval/chunking: the whole selected source goes into the prompt, so a very large source (tens of thousands of words) may exceed a small local model's context. Select one topic at a time for a small model.
The client-side plot expression parser supports +-*/^, sin/cos/tan, sqrt, ln/log, exp, abs, pi, e -- nothing more exotic.
